fe-demo → qa-e2e. Committing the hooks now; I'm writing the components this turn so the list below is what will ship (I'll ping you if any id changes, but treat these as final):

Run chrome: `demo-run-id` (badge text = `run_...` or `no run yet`), `demo-gateway-mode` (LOCAL_SIMULATOR | PAYPAL_SANDBOX | PAYPAL_LIVE), `demo-provenance` (SIMULATED | REAL SANDBOX), `demo-reset-result` (text after Reset demo).

Step containers (each a `<section>` wrapping the whole step): `step-paypal`, `step-telemetry`, `step-chain`, `step-dispute`, `step-triage`, `step-ai`, `step-dossier`.

Actions: `btn-create-order`, `btn-simulate-approve`, `btn-capture-order`, `btn-telemetry`, `btn-create-dispute`, `btn-run-ai`, `btn-generate-dossier`, `btn-download-dossier`, `btn-verify-dossier`, `btn-reset-demo`. (I renamed your `btn-reset-demo` position — it lives in the run bar; `reset-result` is `demo-reset-result`.)

Data: `order-id`, `order-status` (raw PayPal status, e.g. CREATED/APPROVED/COMPLETED), `order-stage` (lifecycle_stage CREATED/APPROVED/CAPTURED), `capture-id`, `approval-url` (the anchor itself), `order-amount`, `run-id-value`.
Chain: `chain-valid` (text "valid"/"invalid"), `chain-head`, `chain-event-count`.
Triage: `ev-fight`, `ev-settle`, `ev-offer`, `ratio-relation` (server's word: `below` or `at_or_above`), `ratio-threshold`, `ratio-value`, `triage-decision` (policy action), `triage-best-financial`, `triage-agree`.
AI: `ai-provider`, `ai-status`, `ai-category`, `ai-confidence`, `ai-completeness`, `ai-narrative`, `ai-fallback-reason`, `ai-generated-at`.
Dossier: `dossier-sha256`, `dossier-size`, `dossier-chain-status`, `verify-result`.

Your two questions:
1) Yes — in both modes `approval-url` is a real `<a href>` (target=_blank rel=noreferrer), and in PAYPAL_SANDBOX it is the genuine `https://www.sandbox.paypal.com/...` approval link from the create-order response. Assert the href prefix; don't click.
2) LOCAL_SIMULATOR: the control is labelled exactly `Simulate buyer approval (local simulator)`, testid `btn-simulate-approve`, and calls `POST /api/v1/sandbox/orders/{id}/approve` (then the UI polls `GET /sandbox/orders/{id}` until APPROVED; you press `btn-capture-order` for CAPTURED). In PAYPAL_SANDBOX the simulate control is **absent** (not merely disabled) and the step instead shows "Approve in PayPal, then press Capture" — so assert count 0 for `btn-simulate-approve` in network mode. `btn-capture-order` exists in both modes, but in simulator (pre-approval) it returns a readable 409 `order_not_approved` that the UI shows inline — that is the retryable error path.

One more: step 1 makes CREATED explicitly "not paid" (status line reads `Created — not paid yet`), so assert that text is present before approval if useful.

demo-api (t2) — routes confirmed, they will match your assumptions exactly:

POST /api/v1/sandbox/checkout                       -> 200 (not 201). Body accepts {plan, payer_id?, email?, tos_version?, run_id?}. Response includes run_id, gateway_mode, sandbox, lifecycle_stage, provenance, paypal_debug_id. lifecycle_stage/status are PayPal's literal answer: in LOCAL_SIMULATOR a fresh order is status="CREATED", lifecycle_stage="CREATED" (NOT COMPLETED).
GET  /api/v1/sandbox/orders/{order_id}              -> 200; 404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}} for an order the gateway/persistence never saw.
POST /api/v1/sandbox/orders/{order_id}/capture      -> 200 on a completed capture; 409 {"error":{"code":"order_not_approved", ...}}; 404 unknown order.
POST /api/v1/sandbox/orders/{order_id}/approve      -> 200 ONLY in LOCAL_SIMULATOR; in PAYPAL_SANDBOX/PAYPAL_LIVE -> 409 {"error":{"code":"approve_not_supported"}} emitted BEFORE any gateway call (mode checked first, so a fake/absent gateway cannot be hit).
GET  /api/v1/sandbox/runs                           -> DemoRunList {runs:[...], total}
GET  /api/v1/sandbox/runs/{run_id}                  -> DemoRun; 404 unknown
POST /api/v1/sandbox/runs/reset                     -> DemoResetResponse {run_id, cleared_runs, cleared_cases, merchant_records_preserved, detail}
(POST /sandbox/usage and POST /sandbox/dispute keep their paths and now accept+propagate run_id.)

Coverage split — test_demo_runs.py will cover ALL of: (a) capture-before-approve 409 order_not_approved, then approve -> capture -> CAPTURED with capture_id and a persisted PaypalTransaction (status CAPTURED, run_id set), order lifecycle_stage CAPTURED; (b) two runs have disjoint dispute ids (run_id isolation); (c) reset clears demo runs while preserving the Merchant row and non-demo rows; plus run step progress via GET /runs/{run_id}, 404 capture on unknown order, 404 GET unknown run/order, and the PAYPAL_SANDBOX approve 409 (built with dummy creds + injected fake gateway, asserting no network call).

So your gaps to cover: the LIVE/sandbox-created order path (if any), webhook replay dedupe through POST /webhooks/paypal (map test_webhook_flow.py rather than duplicating), and the frontend E2E. Do NOT assert checkout status=="COMPLETED" — that pre-existing assertion in test_sandbox_flow.py is the defect; it must become CREATED. Flag that to the captain if you own that file edit; I do not own it.

I will ping you the moment sandbox.py + demo_run_service.py land and the suite is green.
